uncited: This method renders segmented volumetric datasets by "painting" colors derived from segmentation labels directly onto the rendered volume, rather than relying on distinct transfer functions for object separation.

It solves the problem of jagged, sawtooth edges at subvolume boundaries that occur in standard categorical rendering when rays clip voxel corners between samples, delivering higher image quality with smoother transitions.
It sets itself apart from its parent [iso_categorical](4049-iso-categorical.md) by replacing discrete voxel-at-a-time testing with a continuous painting approach that enhances anatomical features.
The method operates on segmented 4D cardiac datasets synchronized with electrocardiogram signals.
It utilizes segmentation labels to acquire specific colors for different anatomical structures.
These colors are then applied to the volume during the rendering process.
The core mechanism involves mapping segmentation data to visual attributes to enhance the visibility of anatomical features while maintaining smooth boundaries between distinct objects.
- Segmented Volume: 3D grid of voxel values.
- Segmentation Labels: 3D grid of integer labels identifying anatomical structures.
- Color Map: Mapping from label IDs to RGB color values.
Acquire segmentation labels for the volume.
Map each unique label to a specific color value.
During ray casting, sample the segmentation labels along the ray.
4. "Paint" the acquired colors onto the rendered volume based on the sampled labels.
Composite the painted colors to produce the final image.
This algorithm was presented in the context of rendering 4D cardiac datasets synchronized with electrocardiogram signals.
It was developed to improve upon previous techniques for dynamic volume rendering and manipulation.

The method was introduced to facilitate image manipulation and image-guided intervention by providing higher image quality and smoother subvolume boundaries compared to using different transfer functions for segmented object separation.
